https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_video_game_console_releases

The usual time between a console's release and the release of it's successor is usually 5 years. Like I said before, last generation lasted a fucking eternity for 360 / PS3 because the systems cost so much money to make that MS and Sony wanted to squeeze as much out of them as they could to get their money's worth. For North America releases:

Nintendo

  • NES: 1985

  • SNES: 1991

  • N64: 1996

  • Gamecube: 2001

  • Wii: 2006

  • Wii U: 2012

  • NX: 2017

Sony

  • PS1: 1995

  • PS2: 2000

  • PS3: 2006

  • PS4: 2013

Microsoft

  • Xbox: 2001

  • Xbox 360: 2005

  • Xbox One: 2013

You can see that the 360 lasting 8 years and the PS3 lasting 7 years before having their successor come out were an anomaly.
